reviews.title: Wow, I paid for this but now it forces me to buy a subscription in order to access what I bought?!?
reviews.text:
The Pillow developers have sunken even lower as of today or very recently. I had paid for the app back before they started their absurd “subscription” for what I can essentially get with an $8 one-time purchase of AutoSleep. Generally I prefer AutoSleep, but it was nice to check in with Pillow too and see how the different algorithms evaluate my sleep. 

This morning I opened Pillow and there is an absolutely unskippable splash screen that only gives the “option” of a forced subscription in order to use what I already paid for— but with some extra “premium” nonsense thrown in for $50 more a year!! What a scam, and if Pillow has sunken this low in order to force the Premium onto people they must be in really bad shape. I am GUESSING that if I agree to their “trial” and then go into Setting of my iOS and immediately cancel that subscription then things will be back to the level I paid for. But Pillow must be calculating that a lot of people either don’t know that and/or will forget to do that and they will have captured plenty of fraudulent extra payments via this trick. It’s a cute program, and I might even be convinced to kick them an extra $10/year for some more features, but $50 more a year for the measuring of my snoring and a lot of blah-blah-blah coaching and tips isn’t in my needs or budget. Forcing paid users to do a trial and then figure out subscription disablement in order to access the app they already paid for should be banned by Apple, it’s unethical.

reviews.title: Sleep Cycle Tracker Doesn’t Work
reviews.text:
Bought this specifically for the function to wake me up at the end of a sleep cycle using my Apple
Watch data. As far as I can tell, setting this feature simply wakes you up exactly 29 minutes before your alarm every day. Every single night I used it during the trial, it would wake me up exactly one minute into the 30 minute window. To me that doesn’t appear to be using any sleep cycle data at all, and completely arbitrary. Perhaps it was just a coincidence but I’m not willing to pay the annual fee to find out. Last night it also randomly wrote sleep data to my watch at 5pm saying I got “poor quality” sleep, when I wasn’t sleeping at all. Just sitting down. Had to go into my health app and manually remove all the data Pillow had written to it, as it seemed to randomly write bad and arbitrary data that spoils the bunch. Other than that, the only other thing it does that Apple Watch’s basic sleep app doesn’t is persistently buzz your watch every 15-30 seconds once the alarm goes off telling you that it’s time to wake up and - far as I can tell - there is virtually nothing you can do to stop it outside of deleting the app, which I did, so I could go back to sleep. Cancelled my trial. Very disappointed as I really wanted this feature to work better than it does.
